sets.relationshipLabel: the thing that lets the action happen
sets.explanation: An oar is what makes rowing possible just as a flipper is what makes swimming possible — each is the enabling part without which the action can't occur.

sets.relationshipLabel: two names for the same thing
sets.explanation: Selkie and seal-folk are two names for the same mythical being, just as pelt and hide are two names for the same animal covering.

sets.relationshipLabel: two ends of one spatial axis
sets.explanation: Shoreline and horizon mark the two visible ends of the sea's breadth, while surface and seabed mark the two ends of its depth — the same kind of axis, read in two directions.

sets.relationshipLabel: a place and the item hidden or stored there
sets.explanation: A chest conceals a stolen sealskin and a rafter conceals a hidden net — each pair names the hiding place and the very object the selkie tales turn on.
